lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: This is the Impossible Sports Network! Live coverage of sports that should not be legal, or possible!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Impossible Sports Network! If it can't be done, we've got the highlights!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Impossible Sports Network. I used to play a sport. It's gone now. Anyway. Here's Chip.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: You're tuned to the Impossible Sports Network, live from Coliseum Zero, in the upper atmosphere! Mind the edge!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Impossible Sports Network! Nobody knows the rules! Everybody knows the score! The score is a color!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Good evening, sports fans, and welcome to Coliseum Zero for tonight's Sunball! I'm Chip Thunderbuckle, alongside the great Doug Steadman. Doug, what a night!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: It's a night, Chip.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And here comes the ball! The ball tonight is a small, polite sun, roughly the size of a melon, and it is glowing beautifully!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: The sun's in good form this season. It's apologizing less.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The referee places it on the center spot! The players are in their oven mitts! And there's the whistle!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And it's kicked! Oh! Oh, the sun says sorry! The sun has apologized to the boot! What a gesture!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Old habit, that. They train it out of them in the junior leagues, but some suns just can't help it.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The Glow Wardens have it now, up the left wing, he's running, he's sweating, everybody's sweating, Doug, it's a sun!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: It's a hot sport, Chip. Always has been.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: He shoots! It's in! It's a goal! The net is on fire! The net is always on fire! The groundskeeper is already bringing out a new one!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Lovely finish. Low, warm, right in the corner.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: We're into the second half here at Coliseum Zero, and Doug, something's happening to the ball!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: It's going down, Chip.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: It's going down! The ball is sinking slowly toward the western goal line, and it's turning a gorgeous orange!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: That's a sunset. It does it every evening. Nobody ever schedules around it.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Can the players do anything?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: No. You can't kick a sun while it's setting, Chip. It's in the rulebook. It's the only thing in the rulebook.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Both teams are just standing there now! They're watching it! Some of them have taken their mitts off! A defender has put his arm round a striker!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Gets everyone, a good sunset.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And it's gone. The ball has set. The stadium is dark. Ninety thousand fans, just sitting quietly in the dark.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Doug, this is the best match I've ever seen.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Play resumes at sunrise. Bring a coat.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Time for tonight's results from around the multiverse! Doug, I'll read them, you explain them!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: I won't.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Sunball! Glow Wardens three, Eclipse United, a warm feeling!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Gravity Polo! The Upward Falcons twelve, the Downward Wolves, yes!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Competitive Waiting! Still waiting! Result expected next spring!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The Backwards Marathon! The winner finished yesterday, and started this morning!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And in Mirror Tennis, it's a draw. It's always a draw. It's been a draw for three hundred years!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Doug, care to explain any of that?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: The Wolves got yes because they asked nicely.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And the final score here at Coliseum Zero tonight was a color! Doug, what color?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: A sort of teal. Fans of the losing side say it was more of a mood.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: We're live at the finish line for the annual Backwards Marathon, where the runners start at the finish and run the course in reverse, until they've un-run it!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Beautiful event, Chip. Very hard on the knees. Backwards.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The runners are lining up at the finish now, wearing their medals, which they'll be handing back at the start! Doug, what makes a great backwards marathoner?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Regret, mostly. You've got to want to go back. And you can't see where you're going. You can only see where you've been.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: That's beautiful, Doug.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: It's a hamstring injury, Chip, is what it is.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The favorite today is Pelham Ostrander, last year's winner, who finished so far behind everyone that he was back at the start before they began!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Great sense of where he came from, Pelham.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The starter raises the pistol, which fires inward! And they're un-off!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Look at them go! Look at them come back! I honestly don't know which it is!

clips.title: The Grand Slow Prix, Live from the Leaf

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: We're live on the leaf at Snail Jams for the Grand Slow Prix, and Doug, the tension is unbelievable!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: They've been on the start line since Tuesday, Chip.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: In lane one, Thistle! In lane two, Old Margaret! And in lane three, the young sensation, Barry, who is wearing tiny headphones and has a very determined look on his face!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Nice shell on Barry.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And they're off!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Thistle is, Thistle is thinking about it! Old Margaret has extended one eye! The crowd can barely breathe!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Tactical race, this. Nobody wants to commit too early.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Barry has moved! Barry has moved approximately one millimeter, and the crowd is losing its mind!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: He's left a lot of trail out there. Too much trail. He'll pay for that in the fourth week.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: We'll be back with more from the leaf next month! Don't go anywhere! Nobody here is!

clips.title: Competitive Waiting: The Bureau Open, Day Nine Thousand

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: We're live at the Bureau of Infinite Queues for day nine thousand of the Bureau Open, the most grueling event in Competitive Waiting!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: It's a mental game, Chip. Always has been.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Two competitors remain! In the blue chair, Agatha Venn, who has been waiting since she was eleven! In the orange chair, the challenger, a man named Clive, who came in to ask for directions!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Clive's got no business being here, Chip. And yet.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And the take a number display has changed! It now reads four billion and six!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Neither competitor has reacted! Neither competitor has reacted! What composure!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Look at Agatha's hands. Folded. Still. She's not even holding a magazine. That's thirty years of discipline, that is.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Clive has picked up a magazine! It's from eleven years ago! He's reading about a holiday he will never take!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Rookie error. Once you're reading, you're waiting for the magazine to end. Different event entirely.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: We'll be back with more waiting in about four years!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: I'm down on the pitch with tonight's ball, the small, polite sun. Sun, congratulations on a terrific match!

lines.speaker: The Ball, a Small Sun
lines.text: Thank you, Chip. I'd just like to thank both teams for kicking me so gently.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: How did it feel out there?

lines.speaker: The Ball, a Small Sun
lines.text: Warm.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: There was that moment in the second half, when you went into the net, and the net caught fire! Talk us through that!

lines.speaker: The Ball, a Small Sun
lines.text: I felt terrible. I always feel terrible about the net. I've sent it a card.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Any message for the fans?

lines.speaker: The Ball, a Small Sun
lines.text: Please wear sun cream, and drink some water. And if anybody's thinking about me, at sunset, I'm fine. I'm just going round.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The sun, everybody! What a professional!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Doug, what a debut! The late substitute, a shadow wearing number zero, no person attached, came on in the eightieth minute and changed the game!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: He played in the gaps, Chip. Went everywhere the light wasn't. I've never seen positioning like it.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: I'm joined now by the player himself. Great game! What's your name?

lines.speaker: Greg, Number Zero
lines.text: Greg.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Greg! Where did you learn to play like that?

lines.speaker: Greg, Number Zero
lines.text: Under people. You learn a lot, under people.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: That winning goal! You were behind the goalkeeper the whole time! He never saw you!

lines.speaker: Greg, Number Zero
lines.text: Nobody ever looks behind them. I was behind someone for forty one years.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Any message for the fans?

lines.speaker: Greg, Number Zero
lines.text: Tell Hollis I'm okay. Tell him I scored.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Who's Hollis?

lines.speaker: Greg, Number Zero
lines.text: He'd know.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Chip, I think that's the shadow off the news.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Greg, everybody! A real shadow of a player! In a good way!

clips.title: World Hide and Seek, Year Forty One

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: We're back at the World Hide and Seek Championship, which has now entered its forty first year! Doug, bring us up to speed!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: The defending champion, Imelda Crane, has not been found. She went to hide in the first year. The seeker counted to a hundred. That was forty one years ago.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And the seeker is still looking!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: He's checked everywhere, Chip. Every cupboard. Every curtain. Under every bed in the Overlap. Very thorough man.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Has anyone considered that she might have simply gone home?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Chip, that is the single most disrespectful thing anyone has ever said on this network.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: I apologize to Imelda, wherever she is!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: She's very good, Chip. That's all you need to know. She's the best there's ever been.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And there's movement! The seeker has just shouted, coming, ready or not! He shouts it every hour! The crowd goes wild every time!

clips.title: The Long Jump, Four Hundred Years In

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Folks, breaking news in the long jump! Ottoline Brisk, who took off in the qualifying round four hundred years ago, is about to pass directly over Coliseum Zero!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Still airborne. Beautiful form. She's barely lost any height.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Everybody look up! There she is! She's waving! Ottoline Brisk is waving to the crowd!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: She's got a sandwich, Chip. Somebody's thrown her a sandwich. That's within the rules.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Doug, when will she land?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Nobody knows. That's the beauty of the long jump. You go as far as you go.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And if she does land, what will her distance be?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Most of the way round, Chip. The judges have had to measure it with the sea.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: There she goes, over the far stand, and out toward the horizon! Ottoline Brisk, everybody! See you next century!

clips.title: Mirror Tennis: The Reflection Takes a Point

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Folks, something historic is happening at the Mirror Tennis Open! For three hundred years, every match in this sport has been a draw, because you play against your own reflection!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Same shots. Same speed. Same score. Purest sport there is, Chip.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: But tonight Vivian Hale is serving for the match, and Doug, her reflection is not serving!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Her reflection is tying its shoelace.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Vivian serves! The reflection isn't even looking! It's in! It's an ace! Vivian Hale has beaten her own reflection!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: No, Chip. Look at the scoreboard.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The scoreboard says, the reflection, one! The reflection has won the point! The reflection was tying its shoelace, and won the point!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Because it didn't care, Chip. First time in three hundred years someone on that court didn't care. Vivian cared too much. She always has.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: That's very deep, Doug.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: I've been there. Not in tennis. But I've been there.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The reflection is leaving the court! It's going for a sandwich! Vivian is still standing there! Vivian is reflecting!

clips.title: Doug's Corner: The Last Game of Cloudball

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: This is Doug's Corner. Chip's getting a sandwich.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: People ask me what Cloudball was. It's hard to explain, now. You'd need a sky like the ones we used to have.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: The goals were clouds. They drifted. You'd get the ball, look up, and the goal would be over the next valley, so you'd run. Whole games happened miles from where they started.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: I played centre half for the Lowland Mists for eleven seasons. Never won a thing. Didn't matter. You were up in the hills with your mates, chasing weather.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: The last game was in the summer of the long drought. We kicked off under one cloud. By half time it was getting thin. By the eightieth minute, you could see through it.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: And then it was gone. The sky went clear, and stayed clear. Nowhere to score.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: We stood there for a bit. Nobody blew the whistle. Somebody's dad brought out oranges.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Anyway. It's a sun for a ball now. Fine. Good sport. Very bright.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: But if you ever see a big, slow cloud going over a field, and you feel like running after it, for no reason. That's Cloudball. You're playing. Go on.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Back to Chip.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: It's the final of Synchronized Existing, folks, and the pair from the Overlap are on the mat!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Lovely pair. Twins. Well. The same person, twice. Which helps.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And they're existing! Look at them exist! Total commitment! They are both, very clearly, here!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Bit of a wobble in the second minute there, Chip. One of them thought about lunch.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Is that a deduction?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Half a point. You can't be thinking about lunch while existing at this level. It's just the existing. Nothing else.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The routine's over! The judges are scoring! Nine point five! Nine point five! And a seven, from the judge who also thought about lunch!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Hypocritical. But that's judging.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: What a performance! Doug, could you do that?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Chip, I've been existing for fifty eight years. Never once been scored. That's the difference between amateurs and professionals.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: It's the Sports Phone-In! Lines are open! Caller, you're on the Impossible Sports Network!

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Hello? Is this the request line?

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: This is the Sports Phone-In! Do you have a sports question?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Well, I'm looking for a song. It goes dum, dum, da dum. And then a man cries.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Bev, is that a chant? Doug, is that a terrace chant?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Sing it again, Bev.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Dum. Dum. Da dum.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: That's every final I ever played in, Bev. That's not a song. That's the sound of the last whistle.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh. Well, can you play it?

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Bev, I'll do you one better! Ninety thousand fans, are you ready? On three! Dum, dum, da dum!

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh, that's lovely. That's not it. But that's lovely.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Gravity Polo, folks, third chukka, and the Upward Falcons are pressing!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Gravity flips every chukka in this sport, Chip. Any minute now.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Falcons on the attack, the rider's lining up the shot, he swings—

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And gravity's flipped! Gravity has flipped! The horses are on the ceiling! The players are on the ceiling! The crowd is on the ceiling, and the crowd is loving it!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Well, the crowd hasn't got a choice, Chip.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The ball is falling upward toward the Wolves' goal, it's going in, it's going in, oh, it's stuck in the floodlights!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: That happens. The lights are the floor now.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Doug, as a former professional, what's the trick to Gravity Polo?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Same as any sport, Chip. Keep your hat on, and know which way is down. And if you don't know, ask the horse. The horse always knows.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: It's halftime! And that means it's time for the Grumbel's Ladders Halftime Report! Up is a choice!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Doug, the stats!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Possession, fifty fifty. Shots on target, four each. Shots at the sun, which is the ball, nine, and the sun has asked everyone to calm down.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And this halftime, a very special guest, the chairman of Grumbel's Ladders himself, Arnold Grumbel! Arnold, what's the halftime entertainment?

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Thanks, Chip. We've put a ladder in the center circle. The tallest one we make. Anyone in the crowd can climb it.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And what's at the top?

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: A view, Chip. Just a nice view. It's a good ladder.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: I see people climbing! There's a lot of them! There's a whole family! They're sitting on the top rung, eating sandwiches!

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: That's all we want, really.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders, everybody! The second half is up next!

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The Tug of War Against Time, folks! Team Present, eight strong lads and lasses, versus next Thursday!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Rope's tied to next Thursday, Chip. Team Present has to pull it closer. Next Thursday pulls the other way, as it always does.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And they're heaving! Team Present is heaving! They've pulled next Thursday to Wednesday! They've got it to Wednesday!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Good technique. Low center of gravity. Don't look at the calendar.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: But oh! Next Thursday's pulling back! It's slipping away! It's next Thursday again! The crowd groans!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: It always gets away, Thursday. You can't rush it.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Doug, has anyone ever actually won this?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Once. A team pulled the holidays all the way into October. Nobody's been happy since.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Transfer news! Big transfer news, folks! The Glow Wardens' star striker, Dex Morrow, has been transferred to a parallel universe!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: For an undisclosed fee, Chip. And a slightly better version of himself.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: That's right! In exchange, the Wardens receive the other Dex Morrow, who is the same in every way, except he passes more, and calls his mother!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Fans are split. Some say it's the same player. Some say the new one's too nice. One man has written a very long letter.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Also in transfer news, the left winger for Eclipse United has become a bird, and is out for the season!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: He'll be missed. He'll also be up there, Chip. Watching.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And the Lowland Pumas' goalkeeper has been transferred to the past, where he'll be playing for a team that won't exist for another three hundred years! Good luck, son!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: He'll be early for training. That's something.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Before tonight's match, folks, the coin toss! Doug, this coin was tossed at the start of the season!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Still up there, Chip. Tossed it in the spring. Very high flip. Nobody's seen it since.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Both captains are standing in the center circle, looking up!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: They've been there since spring. The home captain has grown a beard. The away captain has had a baby. Lovely baby.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The referee's calling it! Heads or tails!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: He's been calling it every day. We'll know when it lands.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Something's coming down! Something is coming down! It's, it's a pigeon. It's a pigeon.

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Pigeon's not a result, Chip.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Kickoff is postponed again, folks! But what an atmosphere!

clips.title: Extreme Staring: Rosalind Teague versus the Void

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Extreme Staring, folks! The champion, Rosalind Teague, against the void!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: The void is undefeated, Chip. Eleven thousand matches. Never blinked once. Hasn't got eyes, to be fair.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Rosalind's at the edge, she's leaning in, she's staring into the void! And the void, Doug!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: The void is staring back, Chip. It always does. That's the problem with the void.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: Four minutes! Five minutes! Rosalind is holding steady! Her eyes are watering! And the void is, the void is studying, apparently! The void has got headphones on!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: It's got exams, Chip. Leave it alone.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: And Rosalind blinks! Rosalind blinks! The void wins again!

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: Gracious in defeat, though. Look. She's left it a biscuit.

lines.speaker: Chip Thunderbuckle
lines.text: The void has taken the biscuit! First time in history! Doug, what does it mean?

lines.speaker: Doug Steadman
lines.text: It means it was hungry, Chip. Studying's hard work.
